blockers.name: missing public after-start loss tests
blockers.detail: Existing runtime test gates a manually submitted private envelope after owner execution and separately tests a public call that expires in the queue. It does not exercise public Handle timeout or cancellation after the real command starts or confirm durable recovery via those public paths; add deterministic gated controls for both operations before retry policy is considered.

separate_inherited_resource_issue.detail: The added public runtime propose_attempt checks Vec length but transfers the entire Vec allocation into the queued envelope; a one-byte vector with arbitrarily large capacity can exceed per-envelope Rust-managed accounting. The pre-existing runtime propose method has the same length-only behavior; the older replication actor checks capacity. Config::managed_bytes accounts bounded command slots and envelope size, and its stated exclusions for allocator overhead/RSS do not exclude live Vec capacity. This is not a newly introduced legacy regression.
separate_inherited_resource_issue.suggested_control: Using a running LocalOwner, pass a one-byte Vec whose capacity exceeds the declared record limit or computed command envelope, then assert both APIs reject before admission, no command/WAL entry is created, and ordinary bounded-capacity input still works. Keep allocations modest (for example a few MiB); no test was run here.
